name: The Cistern of Isse
resident: the wights who come up the stair wet to the knee, and the bell-bearer who stands in the water at the bottom and rings for nobody
story: The Builders' cistern under the Ashgrid: a stair down the well-house's wall into a hall of columns that held the dead city's water, a culvert, and the tank. It has been dry since the Ash Winter, every Sayer who has written of it says so; and there is water in it now, black and still, to the knee in the tank and over the head in the middle, and at the far end the stone where the Builders left their offering to Isse of the Reeds, who taught the stilts, with a jar on it that is full.
unique_object: a jar of water on Isse's offering-stone at the tank's far end, full to the brim, and the water in it moving when nothing else does

features.note: a bucket on a cut rope, wet

rooms.note: the stair going on down, wet to the eighth step
